name: Tsaukambo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 30.
earlier_scan.note: Family sketch includes Tsaukambo (Becking-Dawi) data; PDF not located on journal site

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2012. Some notes on the Tsaukambo language of West Papua. In Hammarström & van den Heuvel (eds.), History, contact and classification of Papuan languages (Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2012, Part I), 165-193. Port Moresby: LSPNG. Open access.
sources.note: p.166: 'There are not enough data in the field notes to enable a phonological analysis' -- only syllable types given, with Baas's stress-marked forms [me'li] 'fire', [nama'ka], [æ'nɔ] 'snake'; p.180: 'We need much more data, on stress patterns and vowel variation..'. No stress-placement rule.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record tsak1250 (Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist, Hughes 2009).
sources.note: Bibliographic: four refs (Hughes 2009, Voorhoeve 2005, Silzer & Heikkinen-Clouse 1991, Versteeg 1983), all 'wordlist or less'; confirms no grammar or sketch exists.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2020. The Greater Awyu Languages of West Papua (Pacific Linguistics 664). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Ch. 2 Phonology covers Aghu, Digul Wambon, Kombai, Korowai only; ch. 1: 'Korowai is the only language in this group [Becking-Dawi] for which there is a grammar.. For the other languages we only have field notes and word lists.' Nothing on Tsaukambo stress.
Lexical data from Hughes (2009) only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wester, Ruth. 2014. A linguistic history of Awyu-Dumut. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
sources.note: Only quotes de Vries 2012 on the Baas notebook and Hughes 2009 being the sole Tsaukambo sources; no Tsaukambo phonology.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2012 Part I, 269-312.
sources.note: Classification/comparative morphology only; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur. Silent.
sources.venue: Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2012 Part I

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 2009. Upper Digul Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-003. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.note: No phonology; sociolinguistic section 'TSAUKAMBO' (pp. 5-7) and Appendix V 239-item wordlist column 'Tsaukambo / Waliburu' in IPA with primary-stress marks (hɑbiˈɑ 'head', ɸɔˈjɔ 'eye', gəˈli 'nose', hɑnduˈsɑmɔ 'stomach', ˈjæmæ 'MM'). No statement on stress placement. Rough tally of marks (my observation, not the source's): 109 final, 56 penult, 23 earlier, 35 monosyllables, 8 unmarked.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-226: rename [kvz] Tsakwambo -> Tsaukambo (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.note: Name-change paperwork citing Hughes's survey; no linguistic content.
Stub; refs Ethnologue 18, Data Pokok Kebahasaan, Hughes 2009; no phonology.

sources.note: The only primary corpus of Tsaukambo beyond Hughes's wordlist; IPA texts carry stress marks, so any future stress statement would come from here. de Vries 2012 excerpted it and judged it insufficient for phonology.
